body.description: Smart Guitar body blank, Explorer-derived ergonomic solidbody. Official CAD length 468.5 mm, derived width 402.85 mm. Thickness 47.0 mm (see CONF-BODY-THICKNESS).

provenance.note: Thickness set to 47.0 mm on 2026-07-27. Enlarged from 44.45 to clear opposed-face web violations among spec-native cavities; 47.0 is the binding requirement from control_cavity (20) against bridge_pickup_route (19), and teensy_io_pocket (20) against neck_pickup_route (19), at min_web 8.0. Briefly held at 51.0 on the strength of an antenna recess that turned out not to be a body cavity at all.

components.role: Linux music brain — JACK + Guitarix/MODEP effects host

provenance.note: Height 18.0 per sg-spec, which the owner ruled canonical. luthiers-toolbox states 17.0 for the same board; see conflict CONF-PI5-HEIGHT. lid_clearance 3.0 mm is an engineering estimate for cable dressing, not a sourced value.

components.display_name: Smart Guitar audio front end (custom HAT)
components.role: Instrument front end, codec, headphone amp, bypass relay and I/O microcontroller on one board

provenance.note: Dimensions are the ENVELOPE from SUBASSEMBLY-SG-AUDIO-FRONTEND-V1, not a measured part — no schematic exists. height_mm is the design TARGET of 24.0, chosen to match the HiFiBerry DAC+ADC it replaces so the pocket does not move; the hard ceiling is 30.0 before the blank must grow. This component also absorbs the Teensy 4.1, which is why no separate MCU pocket remains: that is what makes the electronics fit the solid body.

components.role: One of two identical 2-cell modules. The pair is wired 2S2P for four cells total: double the capacity at the same 6.0-8.4 V.

provenance.note: Pack dimensions per sg-spec. luthiers-toolbox instead lists a single 6000 mAh 18650 cell at 65 x 18.3 mm sited beside the Pi 5. See conflict CONF-BATTERY-PLACEMENT. LABEL CORRECTED 2026-07-28: this read '4x 18650' while its own dimensions describe a TWO-cell pack. A 4-across block is 74.4 wide against the stated 45.0, and a 2x2 block is 37.2 tall against the stated 18.0. The dimensions were right; the label was not. See CONF-BATTERY-CELL-COUNT. BASELINE MOVED TO FOUR CELLS 2026-07-28 by owner ruling. Four 18650s laid flat side by side across the width: 4 x 18.6 = 74.4, plus the same 7.8 of wrap and BMS allowance the two-cell pack carried, gives 82.2. Length and height are unchanged because the cells are unchanged - only how many sit beside each other. Wired 2S2P, so the pack voltage stays 6.0-8.4 V and no board revision follows. SPLIT INTO TWO MODULES 2026-07-28. Four cells in one row is 82.2 wide, giving a 92.2 cavity - deeper than either pod, so it would own the full depth of wherever it sat. As two 2-cell modules the chamber is 55.0, shallower than both pods. This component is now ONE module; two are fitted.

components.role: Thermal management for the Pi 5 in a closed cavity

provenance.note: consumes_cavity_depth is false: the fan vents OUTWARD through the cover rather than sitting inside the cavity depth. RULED by the owner on 2026-07-26 (CONF-FAN-INTRUSION), confirming the modelled configuration. Had it been mounted internally the blank would fail by 6.55 mm, which is why the counterfactual is kept under test. The lid requires vents.

Deliberately NOT placed in any cavity plan. The source sites it 'under Pi 5', where its 3.5 mm would fit inside the Pi's 6 mm standoff gap and consume no additional depth or plan area. That is an assumption, not a derivation, so the part is registered and left unplaced rather than modelled falsely. See conflict CONF-NVME-PLACEMENT.

components.display_name: Pi 5 GPIO to audio front-end ribbon/riser
components.role: Carries the I2S bus between the Pi 5 and the SG_AUDIO_FRONTEND board, which sit side by side rather than stacked

provenance.source_ref: required by CONF-POD-LAYOUT: side-by-side placement forbids header stacking
provenance.note: length_mm 100.0 is a stock GPIO extension ribbon. CORRECTED from 60.0 on 2026-07-27: 60 mm was geometrically IMPOSSIBLE. POD_PI and POD_HAT need at least 72.25 mm centre-to-centre stacked, or 91.00 mm side by side, before their 8 mm walls clear — so a 60 mm ribbon forbade the two pockets from coexisting anywhere, at any body size. That length had been chosen on an AREA argument about the channel's own cost, without checking it was long enough to be buildable. It is registered as a component so pocket separation stays constrained, but the constraint has to be physically possible to be worth anything. NAME CORRECTED 2026-07-28: this component and its role still referred to a HiFiBerry, which was superseded by the custom board in SUBASSEMBLY-SG-AUDIO-FRONTEND-V1. The stale name read as if an off-the-shelf HAT were still in the design. LENGTHENED TO 150.0 ON 2026-07-28 to buy EMC separation. At 100 mm the ribbon, not the body, held the Pi and the analog board 7.0 mm apart; at 150 the constraint moves to the bay and the gap becomes 42.0. A 40-pin GPIO extension ribbon is a stock item at this length - no custom cable, and the HAT form factor was retained from the start so that would remain true. NOTE the cavity plan already carried 150.0 as its stated channel length; the derived 100.0 came from the shorter part, not from a constraint.

cavity_plans.description: Rear-access pocket for the Raspberry Pi 5, with a lid-mounted cooling fan

provenance.note: The one-piece 162 x 64 pod had NO valid position anywhere in the body outline once containment, rim inset and through-body voids were checked. Splitting is not a preference; it is what makes the electronics placeable at the governed body size.

cavity_plans.description: Rear-access pocket for the custom audio front-end board, linked to POD_PI by the GPIO ribbon

provenance.note: Sized from the subassembly envelope rather than from a measured board. Retains the HAT-derived footprint deliberately: matching the part it replaces keeps this pocket stable while the board is still a brief.

cavity_plans.description: Routed channel carrying the GPIO ribbon between POD_PI and POD_HAT

provenance.source_ref: sg-spec rear_wiring_channel (10 x 15 mm) compared against a 40-way ribbon
provenance.note: The derived length of this channel IS the maximum permitted separation between POD_PI and POD_HAT. Set to 100 mm: the pockets need at least 72.25 mm centre-to-centre stacked before their walls clear, so anything shorter forbids the layout outright. Stated dimensions are the spec's generic wiring channel, sized for discrete leads rather than a 40-way ribbon.

cavity_plans.description: Chamber for the 4x 18650 pack and BMS, with power routed to the pod via the spine channel

provenance.note: Modelled as its own chamber because the battery is a separate cavity in sg-spec. Its plan POSITION is unresolved: sg-spec sites it in a bass chamber that a solid body does not have. Depth and footprint are still valid regardless of where it lands. See conflict CONF-BATTERY-PLACEMENT.

conflicts.ruling: INTRA-FILE contradiction, not a cross-repo one: a single file names dual humbuckers in its hardware block and a P90 in its own canonical signal chain. sg-spec contains no P90 reference at all. NOTE these are different pickup CLASSES, not two models of the same thing: a P-90 is a SINGLE COIL, the pickup humbuckers were designed to replace. Consequences split: the audio front-end board is now indifferent to the choice, since its input is specified as headroom plus gain range rather than a level; but pickup ROUTE dimensions still depend on it, and a single coil removes the common-mode rejection that makes an onboard computer tolerable, which is an instrument-level EMC risk recorded in SUBASSEMBLY-SG-AUDIO-FRONTEND-V1.

HEADER-TO-HEADER SPAN GOVERNS, NOT EDGE CLEARANCE. This caught a real error: the first relocation was ruled on edge-to-edge clearance and produced a layout needing 118.8 mm of a 100 mm ribbon - not buildable. The corrected placement spans 89.9 mm, holding 10.1 mm of slack. THE SENSITIVITY IS A CLIFF, NOT A SLOPE: anything from 0 to 15% slack keeps the Pi 71-74 mm from the pickup, but at 20% the packing collapses back to the original 11.6 mm layout. 10% was chosen because zero slack allows no bend radius or connector entry and buys only 2.5 mm of extra clearance. IF A LONGER RIBBON IS SOURCED the constraint relaxes and the search should be re-run; nothing here depends on 100 mm being the only option.

RIBBON LENGTHENED TO 150 mm, ruled 2026-07-28. The reach question stopped being about whether the cable fits and became about what the cable COSTS: at 100 mm it was holding the Pi 7.0 mm from the analog front end, which is the worst EMC geometry in the program and was set by a cable rather than by the instrument. At 150 mm the span available rises from 90.0 to 135.0, the pods separate to 42.0, and the limit moves to the bay width. A stock 40-pin extension exists at this length, so nothing custom follows. THE HEADER-TO-HEADER MEASURE STILL GOVERNS - that lesson is unchanged, and it is why a longer part buys real distance rather than apparent distance.

THE CHOICE IS BINARY, NOT A CONTINUUM: the only real estate far from the coil is the upper bout the deleted neck pickup vacated, and exactly one pocket can occupy it. Either the Pi is far and the pack is close, or the reverse. There is no intermediate layout - the sweep from 12 to 35 mm returns the SAME collapsed result at every step. The Pi keeps the space because it is the dominant aggressor: a 2.4 GHz radio, multi-rail switching regulators and load-dependent current transients, against a pack that is quiet at DC and switches only through its protection and charging circuitry. THE PACK'S EXPOSURE IS REAL AND IS MITIGATED LOCALLY, not geometrically: twisted pack leads, a grounded shield can around the chamber, and charging electronics kept outside the pocket. Those are cheap; a Pi 11.6 mm from a single coil is not fixable at all. Configuration H is the one most likely to falsify it - a charger near full charge drops into pulse-skipping, and the packet repetition rate can fall in the audio band, so H can fail while maximum-current charging passes.

conflicts.ruling:
RULED 4x 18650 IN 2S2P, owner 2026-07-28. The owner ruled two cells earlier the same day, then reopened it once the hollow body removed the cavity constraint that had forced the smaller pack, and ruled four.

THE ORIGINAL CONTRADICTION WAS A LABEL, NOT A DIMENSION. The register said '4x' while its own 80 x 45 x 18 described a TWO-cell pack: an 18650 is 18.6 x 65.2, so four across is 74.4 wide against the stated 45.0, and a 2x2 stack is 37.2 tall against the stated 18.0. Two cells fitted exactly, with 14.8 of length and 7.8 of width left for BMS and wrap. The label has now been made true rather than corrected away.

PACK 80.0 x 82.2 x 18.0, CAVITY 90.0 x 92.2 x 21.0. Four cells laid flat side by side across the width, carrying the same allowances. DEPTH DOES NOT MOVE - still 21.0 - so body thickness is unaffected and POD_HAT continues to govern at 33.0. VOLTAGE DOES NOT MOVE either: 2S2P doubles capacity at the same 6.0-8.4 V, so REQ-POWER-ARCH holds and SUBASSEMBLY-SG-AUDIO-FRONTEND-V1 needs no revision to its electrical envelope. The cost is 37.2 mm of extra WIDTH, plan area 49.5 to 83.0 cm2, and roughly 94 g of added cells.

4S REMAINS RULED OUT: 12-16.8 V would break the board's stated supply range and force a front-end revision to buy exactly the same capacity that 2S2P buys for free.

CARRIED FORWARD: a 2S2P pack needs a BMS that balances two series groups at roughly double the charge current. Ordinary, but a different part from the 2S BMS, and it feeds the peak-draw figures if the charging path shares the board's input.

BUILD IT AS TWO 2-CELL PACKS, NOT ONE BLOCK. Four cells in a single row give a 92.2 mm cavity, which is deeper than either pod and awkward to place - it cannot sit beside them without eating the full depth of whatever region holds it. Split into two 2-cell packs of 90.0 x 45.0 x 21.0, the same four cells are SHALLOWER than either pod and drop in beside or beneath them almost anywhere. Still 2S2P, still four cells, still 6.0-8.4 V, still double the runtime: nothing electrical changes, and no board revision follows. The two parallel strings sit in separate chambers, which is ordinary in laptop and e-bike packs; at these currents the interconnect difference between strings is negligible. BATTERY_CHAMBER therefore becomes TWO chambers rather than one.

BUILT AS TWO 2-CELL MODULES, ruled 2026-07-28. BATTERY_PACK is now one 80.0 x 45.0 x 18.0 module and TWO are fitted, giving two 90.0 x 55.0 x 21.0 chambers instead of one 90.0 x 92.2 x 21.0. Four cells either way, 2S2P either way, 6.0-8.4 V either way - the split is purely about the shape being placeable. Placement is in SG-ELECTRONICS-BAY-V1.

provenance.note: SMART-GUITAR-CAVITY-GEOMETRY-1. Dated read-only snapshot: values were copied here so the derivation stays reproducible if the source repositories change, which they are expected to.

notes: INTERNAL physical geometry record. Contains no cost, price, or manufacturing-time fields by design.

Every cavity dimension in the paired geometry record is DERIVED from this register. Nothing downstream reads a stated cavity dimension, which is why a stale note like 'total_height_mm: 76.0' cannot propagate.
stated_* fields exist only so the derivation can be compared against the source specs. They are never inputs.

The source scan behind this register was BOUNDED and is not exhaustive. It covered sg-spec, luthiers-toolbox instrument_geometry, and tap_tone_pi hardware docs. string_master_v.4.0 was not fully searched. Absence of a conflict record is not evidence that no conflict exists.

min_floor_mm is 8.0 on every cavity: an engineering estimate, not a structural calculation. The pod sits in the lower bout near the control cavity and the battery routing, so the real minimum should come from a structural review under string tension.
The derived pod footprint is a LOWER BOUND. The Hi-Z buffered splitter is required by the canonical signal chain and has no dimensions anywhere, so it could not be included.

This record derives cavity SIZE only. It does not validate cavity POSITION against the body outline, so it cannot detect two cavities colliding in plan or a cavity breaching the perimeter. Plan-level collision checking needs the traced outline and is out of scope. CONF-OPPOSED-FACE-WEB is a concrete instance of what that omission hides.

Pickups, pickup routes, the neck pocket, the bridge, the control cavity, and the output jack are NOT modelled here. This register covers the embedded-electronics cavities only: the pod, the Teensy pocket, and the battery chamber. Pickup disagreements are recorded as conflicts (CONF-PICKUP-TYPE, CONF-PICKUP-ROUTE-DIMS) but no pickup dimension is derived or fit-checked.

Because top-face routes are excluded, the derived body thickness is a LOWER BOUND in a second way: it accounts only for back-face cavity depth plus floor, never for a top-face route cutting toward the same plane from the other side.
